title: Mechanisms
examples: Can you show me an example of a lever in everyday life?
How do gears work together to make something move?
What is the difference between a linkage and a gear?

explain.say: Today we are looking at mechanisms that help things move.
First we will look at levers which use a pivot point.
Next we explore linkages which connect multiple parts together.
Gears are wheels with teeth that mesh together to turn.

draw.text: Gears: Teeth mesh to transfer motion

explain.say: Cams are irregularly shaped pieces that push things up and down.
Think about a bicycle wheel and its gears working together.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a lever and a linkage?
faq.a: A lever usually involves one main pivot point for movement. A linkage connects several moving parts to guide motion.
asks: How do I know if I need a linkage instead of a lever?

faq.q: Do gears always have to mesh with each other?
faq.a: Yes, for them to transfer rotational force, the teeth must connect and move against each other.
asks: What happens if the teeth are too far apart?

faq.q: What is the purpose of a cam mechanism?
faq.a: Cams are used to convert rotational motion into a specific, repeated linear or oscillating motion.
asks: Why are cams used in engines?

faq.q: Can I use simple machines to build a complex mechanism?
faq.a: Yes, most complex mechanisms are built by combining simple machines like levers and gears.
asks: Do I need to know all the simple machines?
Can I combine a lever and a gear?

faq.q: How do I calculate the ratio between two gears?
faq.a: You compare the number of teeth on the two gears to find the ratio of speed or force.
asks: Is the gear ratio always bigger than one?
Does the size of the gear matter more than the teeth count?

facts: Levers use a rigid bar and a pivot point.
Linkages guide motion using connected rods and pivots.
Gears transfer motion through meshing teeth.
Cams convert rotary motion into other types of motion.

quiz.say: A pair of scissors uses which simple machine principle?
quiz.why: Scissors operate by pivoting around a fixed point, which is the definition of a lever.

wrong.1: Gears require teeth to mesh, which scissors do not have.
wrong.2: Cams need an irregular shape to push, which scissors lack.
wrong.3: While they are connected, the primary action is based on a single pivot point.

quiz.say: If a small gear turns one full rotation, what happens to a large gear connected to it?
quiz.show: Small gear turns 1 time; Large gear turns less.

options.show: It will turn less than one full rotation.
options.say: It will turn less than one full rotation.

options.show: It will turn the same amount.
options.say: It will turn the same amount.

quiz.why: The ratio of the teeth means the larger gear must travel a greater distance to complete one turn.

wrong.1: If they turned the same, the force transfer would not be balanced.
wrong.2: This would only happen if the large gear was connected to a much smaller one.
wrong.3: The connection ensures continuous, though altered, movement.

quiz.say: A mechanism that converts the turning motion of a wheel into a straight up-and-down push is best described using:
quiz.why: The specific, non-uniform shape of a cam is designed exactly to create this type of controlled, repeating motion.

wrong.0: Gears primarily transfer rotation to other rotating parts.
wrong.1: Linkages guide motion, but the cam is the specific component causing the push.
wrong.3: Levers rely on a fixed pivot point, not a changing profile shape.
